hook_text: A seven-metre ramp on an A4 page. Five kinds of line, one scale, and sizes a builder can trust.
clip_script: Five lines. Dark: what you see. Feint: your helper lines. Dashed: an edge hiding behind something. Wavy: a break where you cut the middle out. Chain, long short long short: a centre, or where you slice the object open. Now the ramp, 7 200 long, page 297. Scale 1:50: divide by 50, 144 millimetres. The riser, 150, becomes 3. Write 1:50 in the title block. Then dimensions: the real sizes, in millimetres, no unit, once each, outside the shape, number above the line, arrows at the ends. The builder reads 7 200 and never touches a ruler. The scale is for you; the dimensions are for them.
visual_style: Whiteboard showing five line samples labelled, a ramp shrinking onto a page outline with 1:50 appearing, then a dimension being drawn part by part.
pacing: Five lines fast, scale with one calculation, dimension built in four parts.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and dimension one object on your desk at 1:2.
